en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: {city} runs on {industries}, and the first three of those buy slowly. A prospect finds you, reads everything you have published, forwards it to two colleagues, and contacts you weeks or months later, often through a form that credits whatever they clicked last. Judge a campaign here on a 30 day window and you will switch off the thing that was actually working.

That pattern favours being findable and credible over being loud. The businesses that do well in {city} tend to be the ones that have published something worth forwarding: a real explanation of how the work is priced, what the process looks like, and what goes wrong. That is an SEO and content argument more than an advertising one, and it is cheap here because so few competitors are doing it.

The market is also small enough that reputation travels. {city} is roughly a quarter of a million people and the business community is smaller than that. Advertising that overpromises gets found out fast, and the same word of mouth that punishes it rewards anyone whose website matches what they actually deliver.

en.servicesIntro: Same three services everywhere I work. What changes in {city} is the measurement window, because a market that takes two months to decide cannot be judged on a month of data.

services.title: Google Ads Management
services.body: For {city} that means a longer attribution window before anything gets judged, targeting that covers the southern part of the province rather than the city alone, and spend cut off searches that were never going to convert. Useful here, but rarely the first thing I would fix.

services.title: SEO Consulting
services.body: Usually where I would start in {city}. Long buying cycles mean people research before they contact anyone, and thin local competition means the pages that answer those questions can rank quickly. Technical fixes first, then the content your buyers are already looking for.

services.title: AIO Consulting
services.body: Being the {city} business ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews name when someone asks for a recommendation. That matters more in a slow, research-heavy market, because the research now often starts inside a chatbot. Cheapest of the three and one-time.

area.nearbyBody: The natural catchment runs well past the city. I work with businesses in {nearby} on the same terms.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

faq.q: Our sales cycle is months long. Can you even measure that?
faq.a: Yes, and it is the main thing I would set up first in {city}. That means a longer attribution window, tracking that survives someone leaving and coming back weeks later, and reporting that counts qualified enquiries rather than clicks. Without it you are guessing, and the guess usually punishes the channel that did the early work.

faq.q: Should we run ads at all, or just do SEO?
faq.a: In {city} I would often start with SEO and add ads once you know which enquiries are worth paying for. That is not a rule, and if you sell something urgent then paid search comes first. I will tell you which on a call rather than selling you both by default.
Yes. I work across the province and there is a page for Saskatoon as well as one for Saskatchewan generally. If you sell province-wide, the {region} page is probably the more useful starting point.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
